notes: Archived BYU Mormon Literature & Creative Arts person page for Mark Twain: a short biography about his place in Mormon literature (Roughing It), an alias and a one-item work table. The single listed work (Huck Finn and Tom Sawyer among the Indians, 2003) is actually Lee Nelson's completion of Twain's unfinished sequel, credited to Twain as author.

activity_place.raw: Twain describes his visit to Utah

description.value: Mark Twain (1835-1910), the famous American writer, earned a place in the history of Mormon literature as a humorist about nineteenth-century Mormon culture and as a minor critic of The Book of Mormon. In chapters 12-16 of Roughing It, Twain describes his visit to Utah and provides, among other commentary, a humorous defense of Mormon polygamy (Mormon women were so ugly that polygamy was an act of charity). Twain is (in)famous in Mormon circles for having said that the Book of Mormon is "chloroform in print"...
